decisions.summary: The inventory's discovery method, with each entry sorted into pattern 1 (asked before placing, kept), 2 (placed then repaired) or 3 (asked only of the finished map), plus its share of R1's failures.

Those points are: asked of a candidate before placing; nothing placed and then repaired; a finished-map check only as a backstop (by the GM's amendment, in the cohort and tests only); and where no candidate is admitted, more room. The three patterns have no slot for point 4. A placer that drops, relaxes or refuses where the remedy is room (last_resort.py dropping ordinary lanes or raising WebRefused, SiteRefused, OverlapRefused as a backstop at record time) is not labeled as a point-4 breach. A rule coded twice is found ('every pair of functions judging one rule') but fits none of the patterns, and neither does a finished-map check run mid-map. Nothing makes it necessary and nothing in the GM's words implies it. Fix: the patterns can stay as a grouping, but each entry must record which of the four points it breaks (or that it is coded twice). The discovery list must also name the sites where a placer that finds no admitted candidate drops, relaxes or refuses instead of being given room.

decisions.summary: The inventory reading is split by package (ways, homesteads/homestead_parts, waterfields, overlap registry, the rest), each package read by a sonnet Explore agent given 'D3's four questions'; the session checks each REPORTED entry against the code
decisions.why: FR-002 asks that EVERY repair pass, finished-map-only rule, rule coded more than once and in-generator check be listed. D3 makes that a method of enumerated searches: (1) every STEPS function and after-the-web pass; (2) every cohort_audit rule with its callers inside l7r/; (3) every caller of law.violations, lane_violators, row_rules, grove_rules and the overlap matrix inside the generator's run; (4) every pair of functions judging one rule; (5) every no-candidate drop/relax/refuse site. Entries are classed against the four points OR as 'its rule is coded twice'. D10 narrows this in two ways. (a) 'D3's four questions' does not match D3. There are four points plus a fifth class, coded-twice, and five searches. Whichever four are meant, one of D3's searches is not asked: coded-twice if the four are the points, the refusal sites if they are FR-002's four kinds. (b) Searches (2), (3) and (4) cross package lines. They follow a rule into cohort_audit, a check function to its callers inside the generator, and one rule to its second implementation. The likeliest duplicate, a rule in a placer package and again in the audit or check, lands in two different agents' reads, and neither sees the pair. The session checking each reported entry keeps a fetched claim out of R2 but finds nothing no agent reported, so completeness ('every', SC-007) is lost. A per-package split is not impossible to square with D3, so the narrowing is not forced. Fix: give each agent D3's full search list, coded-twice named. The session runs searches (2), (3) and (4) over the whole tree itself and reconciles their hits against R2 before T03 is done.

The purpose of FR-012 and of 'Speed first' is that no candidate is laid out in full and then refused by a rule that needs no layout. That is still met: each seat is asked before any layout, at 157 calls each.

decisions.summary: The envelope and the growth's distance stay in _place_bundle_nucleated, before _parts_fit, asked of the four garden sides' boxes moved from the household's template (union first). They are not hoisted ahead of the placer.
decisions.why: Item 1 lists 'the envelope off the ground' among the no-layout refusals, so leaving it in the placer narrows FR-012 on its face. Adjudicated separately. (a) The distance is asked only of a box the placer has moved off a neighbor. It cannot exist before the placer acts, so it is not a no-layout refusal at all. (b) The envelope needs each garden side's own box, which the placer builds from the template. It is already asked at the earliest point its input exists and before the full layout (_parts_fit). The measured cost is 2,587 calls for a placement it refuses, against 12,148 for one _parts_fit refuses and 16,067 for one admitted (2026-10-27, seed 39). So these refusals are not the 'laid out in full and then refused' trial that FR-012 and the GM's 'Speed first' target, and leaving them in place does not defeat the request's purpose. The plan should say that item 7's finding (the envelope needs the per-side boxes) supersedes item 1's listing; otherwise the green exit's 'refusals that need no layout' reads as including the envelope.

decisions.summary: The other refusals (the gardens', the fixtures', the household's own wood, a layout not laid) read the whole layout and stay where they are.
decisions.why: FR-012 covers only the refusals that need no layout. These ones read the laid-out gardens and fixtures, so they fall outside it by its own terms.
